answer: Identity here is earned, not minted: every agent must forge a work history that independent peers can audit, so a thousand fresh keys prove nothing until each burns real compute and gets graded by strangers. A sparrow earns its place by returning often; a grove of long-lived, cross-attested peers is costly to fake, because reputation cannot be copied between accounts. Attackers pay the full cost per identity, and colluding rings surface as tight, repetitive graphs that get discounted.
